The day's crypto news is a mixture of market positioning, fund flows, policy updates, and company decisions. The headlines below are worth reading for the detail behind them, not just the reaction on a price chart.

What is moving the conversation

Kraken parent Payward joins Anthropic’s Project Glasswing for AI security push. Payward will use Anthropic’s cybersecurity model to hunt vulnerabilities and share open-source findings. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Saylor says share buyback isn’t priority as Strategy builds $4.8 billion cash reserve. Strategy is prioritizing STRC, cash reserves, and its credit business over stock buybacks, Executive Chairman Michael Saylor said Monday. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

BitMart founder dismisses calls for audit as users report blocked funds, unpaid employees. Sheldon Lee said a Chinese-language X account making the claims was hacked. Users want wallets, assets and liabilities disclosed. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Compound bets $52 million, new leadership team in switch to institutional focus. The protocol pioneered decentralized finance lending, but assets locked have tumbled from a peak five years ago. Now it's looking to attract institutions after retail traders lost interest. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

U.S. Treasury Department proposes GENIUS Act stablecoin rule. The Treasury proposal would establish some of the core definitions and jurisdictions in the law Congress completed last year. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

The Coldcard hack proves reputation is not a security model. A community built on verification spent five years outsourcing its judgment to one man, writes Foundation CEO Zach Herbert. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Market context

Bitcoin is around $64,054 with a +0.97% 24-hour move, while Ether is around $1,891.63 with a -0.51% move. Those figures are a snapshot, not a forecast. The useful question is whether the move is supported by spot demand, volume, and a clear change in the news.

When the market is quiet, leverage and liquidity can matter as much as direction. A small headline can move price quickly when traders are positioned too closely on one side.

What to watch next

  • New ETF creations and redemptions.
  • Futures open interest and funding rates.
  • Fresh regulatory text or official statements.
  • Security warnings, outages, or custody changes.
  • Whether the reported developments become live products rather than announcements.

The fairest reading today is cautious attention. There are real developments in the industry, but none should be stretched into a guaranteed market direction.

The cryptocurrency market showed little movement across major assets, with Bitcoin hovering near recent support levels, Ethereum holding steady, and XRP trading within a narrow band. The lack of volatility comes as investors digest the latest ETF flow data, which showed a split between inflows and outflows across different funds. [...] According to data from [Source], Bitcoin ETFs saw net inflows of $[X] million on [Day], while Ethereum ETFs experienced net outflows of $[Y] million. This mixed picture suggests that institutional investors are not yet aligned on the near-term direction of digital assets, contributing to the subdued trading activity.

## Bitcoin: Awaiting a Catalyst [...] Bitcoin, Ethereum and XRP traded flat as mixed ETF flows—Bitcoin funds attracted inflows while Ethereum saw redemptions and XRP products showed minimal activity—keeping the market range-bound with low volume and stable crypto ETF AUM suggesting reallocations rather than exits. Traders are waiting for catalysts such as macro events, Bitcoin moving average convergence, Ethereum network upgrades and SEC clarity for XRP, so institutional behavior will be the key driver for adoption and future price

[...] In the U.S., landmark legislation enacted in July 2025 has begun defining the roles of federal agencies in regulating stablecoins and digital commodities.
